$comment: M99 build-time compatibility baseline. The verdict comes from `sinceChromium` only: <= 99 means the Huawei M99 engine already ships it (recorded as a note, never blocking), > 99 blocks, and "unverified" warns unless --strict. `since` is the ES edition or proposal status and explains the history; it never decides. `allow[]` paths are prefixed to the scan root and matched by prefix; `expires` is an ISO date and a stale entry fails the gate. Workflow: plugins/COMPAT.md.

forbiddenApis.name: Array.prototype.at
forbiddenApis.note: ES2022 is the edition, Chromium 92 is the engine: inside M99. An ES-year threshold would have flagged 52 call sites that need no change.

forbiddenApis.name: Array.prototype.findLast
forbiddenApis.note: ES2023 edition, Chromium 97 engine: inside M99.

forbiddenApis.name: Array.prototype.findLastIndex
forbiddenApis.note: ES2023 edition, Chromium 97 engine: inside M99.

forbiddenApis.name: Array.prototype.with
forbiddenApis.note: Excludes the fluent builder form `this.with({ ... })`; a plain `x.with(i, v)` call is the array method.

forbiddenApis.name: Object.hasOwn
forbiddenApis.note: ES2022 edition, Chromium 93 engine: inside M99.

forbiddenApis.name: structuredClone
forbiddenApis.note: Web API, not an ES feature: Chromium 98, so the Worker baseline includes it.

forbiddenApis.name: RegExp.escape
forbiddenApis.note: Milestone approximate (V8 13.6 train); the verdict only needs a value above the 99 threshold.

forbiddenApis.name: RegExp v flag
forbiddenApis.note: Heuristic: the constructor form requires only valid flag characters, the literal form requires the opening slash to follow an operator or bracket.

forbiddenSyntax.name: Logical assignment (??=)
forbiddenSyntax.note: ES2021 edition, Chromium 85 engine: inside M99, recorded so the family stays covered.

forbiddenSyntax.name: Decorator
forbiddenSyntax.note: No Chromium version ships decorators natively, so there is no milestone to pin: warns by default, blocks under --strict, and `erasableSyntaxOnly` in tsconfig.json already rejects the transform.

forbiddenSyntax.name: import assertions (assert { type: })
forbiddenSyntax.note: The assertion form shipped, was renamed to attributes and no longer parses; whether the Huawei build accepts it is unconfirmed, so it warns and blocks only under --strict.
